body:
Hello, thank you for opening a pull request.

Whether this PR breaks our rules really hinges on whether you now fully understand the change, and whether it is "substantial".

We can't judge the first so you'll need to clarify it. As a rule of thumb, you "understand" the change if you could rewrite it without AI assistance.
Whether the code is "substantial" is walking the line so I'll leave that to area maintainers to judge.

Your PR description is also not very useful to understand the problem and the solution. It reads more like narration than description, and you dumped an AI output in there (which is separately forbidden in our rules). Please rewrite it (using our PR template).

How many people in the world understand this specific spaghetti shader code? Five? (No affront, that's just the fate of shader code) Do they even still or have they forgotten? 

At first I did not understand one bit of the explanation. I questioned every sentence, tried to throw counterintuition and counter examples at it, some claims I verified by looking at the code or testing things in Godot. But some explanations and claims I simply had to take at face value, after asking why, why why not that, why is that.

Of course I read the PR template and made sure that everything in it was answered.

The "AI dump" is the result of this process and me requesting a certain level of depth for a potential reviewer. I don't know what the correct depth for the reviewer for this specific topic is. I can supply a much more in-depth AI explanation including my challenges/scrutinization to it; but if you really want to I can also write a confident and human sounding explanation that totally hides away all of the rest risk/uncertainties that arise from having learned this from an AI and that my understanding is based on taking some background explanations of the AI for face value.

Could I have written the code? I have a PhD in AI applied to Robotics/Computer Graphics but I have never touched any production shader code. Could you have discovered America if someone told you where to sail? Now I can maybe. In six months without AI? Probably not.

I am a senior engineer myself, I have fight with AI written PRs myself and I get that nobody wants 17 file spanning 2000 line AI-written GUI code. But that's a one-file-20-line fix in shader code, the closest thing to assembler that humans still write manually. AI will always have a better understanding than all but maaaybe the five people involved in maintaining this code.

So In essence, yes I understand what the AI wants to tell me, no I don't understand it to a level from independent sources and self-exploration that I, a very sceptical guy, would like to. But I'm not spending three days to manually debug 2000 lines of contextual shader code when I have seen the effective 10-line fix working and the code+explanation makes enough sense to me that I think it is worth risking to waste your time.

So please tell me if you still want me to write a human dunning kruger version of the explanation or if I can help you with anything else, for example more tests.
Just to clarify: are you saying the whole bugfix should be one line, or are you saying some of these lines should be merged to one line?

> Hi, I am one of those "5 people" that actually understand this code. I can confidently say that this code is not in a mergable state.

Hi, lucky you, I think that's fine, I think that's the process and happens with many PRs

> First look at changes like this:
> 
> ```
> 	// Keep direct vertex-computed specular separate from image-based lighting.
> 	// Directional shadows must not attenuate environment/reflection-probe light.
> 	vec3 vertex_specular_light = specular_light_interp.rgb;
> 	specular_light = vertex_specular_light;
> ```
> 
> It doesn't take shader expertise to see that this code adds nothing since the original code was `specular_light = specular_light_interp.rgb;`. It just adds needless verbosity and needless comments because AI likes to do that.

I'm sitting here for a while now and try to figure out if this is some kind of hyperbole or if you really think the code adds **nothing**. It obviously adds the variable `vertex_specular_light` which is (how I understand it) a necessary element of this fix. The new `vertex_specular_light` is kept in sync with `specular_light` _at some places_ but it diverges at others, specifically the accumulation of indirect reflections is only applied to the original `specular_light`. Yes I also feel like that is awkward, but my understanding is that that is the only way to monkey patch this and introducing a mechanism to not make `specular_light` accumulate indirect reflections would be the bigger change. But here I am actually not 100% sure. (Edit: I added a commit fo this variant as well at the bottom.)

I kind of figured that you might dislike the comment breaking the zen flow of 2000 lines of comment free shader code, I am happy to take it out, but it accurately describes why `vertex_specular_light` is introduced.

So if we ignore the comment, what is left to critique essentially sums up to the end result difference between
```
 vec3 vertex_specular_light = specular_light_interp.rgb;
 specular_light = vertex_specular_light;
```
and
```
 vec3 vertex_specular_light = specular_light_interp.rgb;
 specular_light = specular_light_interp.rgb;
```

Maybe it is an unnessary change, maybe it is clearer semantics to set them both equal, I think both can be argued and its far away fom AI hallucination.

> Our expectation is that these sort of hallucinated changes by the AI is removed before a PR is made since it wastes maintainer time to have to review it. In fact, our AI policy specifically mentions this (https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pull_request_guidelines.html#for-contributors). You, as the PR author, need to be able to read the code, understand it, and vouch for it.

I wrote that I read through the code at least five times and that I do understand it to a degree. I wanted to express a caveat that there are limits to it and I of course also have legit trust issues when an AI explains something to me.

> 
> Most of this PR is similar empty code changes that do nothing but waste my time.

Again, I do not know if hyperbole or misunderstanding. For example, yes, you could write


```
		vec3 specular_scale = specular * metallic * albedo * 2.0;
		specular_light *= specular_scale;
#ifdef USE_VERTEX_LIGHTING //ubershader-runtime
		vertex_specular_light *= specular_scale;
#endif
```
closer to the original code (via three added lines) like

```
		specular_light *= specular * metallic * albedo * 2.0;
#ifdef USE_VERTEX_LIGHTING //ubershader-runtime
		vertex_specular_light *= specular * metallic * albedo * 2.0;
#endif
```
And yes, you will end up with a slimmer patch size, but as the end result I can defend both. You might find it quicker to understand that they are both multiplied by the same amount and I could imagine a compiler might find the first one easier to optimize.

> 
> The actual substance of this PR is three code additions
> 
> ```
> vec3 indirect_specular_light = specular_light - vertex_specular_light;
> ...
> vertex_specular_light *= mix(vec3(1.0), light_attenuation, specular_light_interp.a);
> ...
> specular_light = indirect_specular_light + vertex_specular_light;
> ```
> 
> Doing basic algebraic substitutions, it reads as
> 
> ```
> specular_light = specular_light - vertex_specular_light + vertex_specular_light * mix(vec3(1.0), light_attenuation, specular_light_interp.a);
> ```
> 
> So we can see what it is doing is ensuring that the shadow term is only applied to the direct lighting coming from the vertex and not to the indirect lighting coming from the sky.
> 
> Unfortunately, this is the wrong way to make this change. It should be a single line of code. This change makes the code more complicated for no reason and just obfuscates what the actual change is.

This explanation is roughly what the AI-vomit says, btw. The whole fix is defintely not a one line. [For the fun of it AI golfed a solution in three lines](https://github.com/jejay/godot/commit/538be8c34304ae7b58c5450b0edfdff74b733adc), but I highly doubt that this is what you want. You are obviously right if you mean that the above three lines can be merged into one. I slightly disagree that splitting them up into three lines makes it unreadable, I would even argue that the explicit `indirect_specular_light` variable introduction (optmized away in the compiler anyway) makes it clearer and it propbably even helped you understand what is going on. But If you want to have it in one line, your call, this can be easily discussed and changed. I am just saying the way you are reacting to it is a bit over the top.

> Normally if I saw a PR like this (minus the AI-vomit description) I would assume the contributor was new to programming and I would give them feedback to help them improve as a developer. But in this case there is no one to help. The AI doesn't learn from its mistakes and I have no interest in prompting your AI to get it closer to non-spaghetti code. This is a clear violation of our AI policy and is overall terrible code, so I don't see any path towards merging this. 


The bug was introduced in cc2d862733f402bb2147367ff4dc955dac4d9e1f by yourself in 2019, which landed in Godot 3.2 stable. For six years there was a graphics glitch on any Android or iOS export with Godot 3 GLES3 that pops into your eye the moment you start the offical 3D Platformer Demo.

Is this correct? This is the first question that I was asking implicitly in this PR, and also: Is this fix conceptually the right one? I think this needs to be discussed first, then it makes sense to me to discuss code beauty.

As a side note, I am programming semi- and professionally for 20 years up until now. Maybe you are one of the few exceptions, just like there are still a few freaks out there who still hand write assembler, but in general I would not recommend tying my ego to the idea that I am smarter than these machines.

> If you decide to take another stab at fixing this issue, feel free. But please open a new PR and ensure that the contained code reaches at least minimal standards of code quality.

Do you want [this](https://github.com/jejay/godot/commit/cab49611d6da8bc8a7e2d64b86ac93ac96fb7334) or do you want [that](https://github.com/jejay/godot/commit/5c8dd573dd0da069873c0de0268307bcdb2250ed)? The first one is this idea reduced to eight lines, the other one is instead introducing a new variable for indirect specular from the very top. Maybe this is more elegant, but my AI says this might also be a bit slower for the non-vertex-mode case. I don't know, your call.
